abstract: Long-horizon agents compact their history to continue within a finite context window, but a textual summary alone may not support every subsequent decision. We introduce Remory, a neural memory network that supplements the summary with a bounded sequence of soft memory tokens. Given the history and summary, the network learns to generate tokens that help a frozen LLM approximate the continuation it would produce with the full history. The tokens are conditioned on the summary and appended after it, forming an analogue of a residual connection along the sequence dimension. On SummHay, Remory improves source attribution at nearly unchanged insight coverage and approaches the full-context joint score using only 5.2% of the input positions. Across long-horizon agent benchmarks, Qwen3.8-27B and GLM-5.3-Flash show consistent gains with residual memory. Both models also exhibit substantially fewer repeated tool outputs and tool errors on BrowseComp and Terminal-Bench 2.1.

sections.body: Long-horizon agents replace earlier interaction with a textual summary to free context space, as Claude Code and Codex do with /compact. The authors argue that a summary may not support every later decision, and that the earlier context needed cannot always be listed in advance. Remory trains a neural memory network to generate a bounded sequence of soft memory tokens, appended after the summary, so that a frozen LLM approximates its full-history continuation. The section cites a sawtooth input-length pattern across compactions (Figure 2a) and draws an analogy to hippocampal indexing. Exact records remain available through archive and file-retrieval tools. The section also states that frontier scores are published context only.
sections.heading: Introduction
sections.headline: Summaries alone may miss context needed later, so Remory adds learned memory tokens after a summary.

sections.body: Memory is built from the previous summary, any prior residual memory, and new interaction. A network predicts memory vectors in parallel using learned queries and gated cross-attention to the summary. Each block of up to 1,024 source positions yields 64 soft tokens, and hierarchical compression caps the final memory at 4,096 slots. Training has two stages. Stage I reconstructs a source passage from soft memory. Stage II trains the student to match the teacher's predictions for the same next response, and the memory encoder never receives that response. The loss is student-to-teacher reverse divergence, and only the memory parameters are updated. The memory networks have 1.94B and 1.502B trainable parameters for Qwen3.8-27B and GLM-5.3-Flash.
sections.heading: Residual Memory
sections.headline: A memory network trains soft tokens so a frozen actor matches its full-history continuation.

sections.body: On SummHay, summary plus residual memory reaches a joint score of 43.39, against 39.84 for summary alone and 43.41 for raw context. Citation F1 rises from 56.98 to 61.03, and coverage is 67.95 against 67.55. Mean inputs are 5,024 positions with memory, which the text gives as 5.2% of raw-context positions. Qwen gains 9.8 points on AutomationBench and 7.6 on JobBench over five runs. GLM gains 3.3 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 4.1 on BrowseComp, each from one run. Repeated tool outputs fall by 17.9–29.8% and errors by 25.3–49.7% across the four actor–benchmark pairs. Limits: the first-action study covers 488 paired actions and judges plans rather than outcomes.
sections.heading: Experiments
sections.headline: Residual memory raises SummHay joint score and agent scores while reducing repeated tool outputs and errors.

sections.body: The section places Remory among agent memory systems that combine summaries with retrieval, such as ReadAgent, MemGPT, ReSum, and AgentFold, and keeps their textual checkpoint and retrieval interface. It also relates the method to continuous-representation work, including AutoCompressors, Gist Tokens, and ICAE, and to recurrence and memory-token approaches. The stated distinction is that Remory applies a predictive criterion to the information gap a summary leaves, training the supplement through a frozen actor's continuation predictions. The section reports no new experiments.
sections.heading: Related Work
sections.headline: Remory extends summary-plus-retrieval memory with a continuous representation learned from the checkpoint.

sections.body: The conclusion restates the design: a readable summary, soft tokens that carry additional predictive information, and retrieval for exact records. Reconstruction followed by summary-conditioned continuation trains this interface while leaving the actor unchanged. The authors cite improved source attribution, higher agent scores, and preferred next actions as support for the residual formulation. These claims rest on the within-actor comparisons and benchmarks reported earlier, and the section adds no new measurements. Published frontier scores are presented only as context.
sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.headline: Attribution, agent scores, and preferred next actions support the residual formulation as a bounded supplement.
